title: The trim bound: gaps of 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0 mm are sewn across, 1.2 mm and up are trimmed
description: Eight 5 x 5 mm red fill squares with gaps of 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 1.8 and 2.0 mm: PE-DESIGN 11.50 sews the three shortest gaps across as plain stitches (no jump at all) and trims the four others (needle-to-needle moves of 2.42 mm and more). The squares' y position is OpenStitch's choice. OpenStitch's optimized exit and entry points lie on the squares' edges where PE-DESIGN's lie 0.5 mm inside them and 1 mm apart in y (its moves are sqrt((gap + 1)^2 + 1) mm), so the squares are drawn at PE-DESIGN's needle-to-needle moves and the trimming rule is compared at equal moves; where PE puts its exit and entry inside the edge is the fill track's open item.

evidence.note: PE-DESIGN 11.50 reference machine/machine-trim-bound.pes (pe-refs-3, 2026-10-28): 698 stitches, 4 trims on moves of 2.42, 2.69, 2.97 and 3.16 mm; the 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0 mm gaps have no jump.

references.make: Import an SVG (100 x 100 mm) with eight 5 x 5 mm red squares at x = 10, 15.5, 21.3, 27.3, 33.5, 40, 46.8, 53.8 mm (gaps 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 1.8, 2.0 mm), as Fill Stitch at PE-DESIGN's import defaults (multi-needle machine type, Jump Stitch Trimming on); change nothing. Save with Save As as PES (PE-DESIGN 11's default PES version) under the file name given, and record the PE-DESIGN version, the date, the operating system and every setting you changed in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json (see docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md).

measurements.evidence: every interior move is a trimmed jump (as many moves as trims); a gap PE-DESIGN does not trim is sewn across as a stitch, never left as a plain jump
PE-DESIGN's count (its fill rows join differently from OpenStitch's, the text-fill item of the audit)
